blocks.raw: The **Trigger Block** is the starting point of the dataflow, where you can configure the dataflow with the API method type (e.g., POST, GET) and a custom API endpoint.
blocks.text: The Trigger Block is the starting point of the dataflow, where you can configure the dataflow with the API method type (e.g., POST, GET) and a custom API endpoint.

blocks.raw: Once configured, the API cURL is created based on the configuration here. You can use either the API cURL or the endpoint to invoke the dataflow. The trigger block appears automatically after you create the dataflow.
blocks.text: Once configured, the API cURL is created based on the configuration here. You can use either the API cURL or the endpoint to invoke the dataflow. The trigger block appears automatically after you create the dataflow.

blocks.raw:
1. From the dataflow canvas, hover on the Trigger Block and click on the edit icon.
2. In the **API Method** field, select the HTTP method (GET, POST, or PUT).
3. In the **API URL** field, enter the unique endpoint for the dataflow.
4. *(optional)* To include a path parameter in the URL, prefix the variable name with a colon (`:`). For example, to include `customerId` as a path parameter, write it as `:customerId` in the URL. Use path parameters when you work with APIs that support dynamic values in the URL. This is helpful when making multiple API calls that have different values, such as different customer IDs. Instead of creating a separate cURL command for each value, you can reuse the same endpoint by replacing the path parameter.
5. Click **Done.**

blocks.raw: For example, the below API cURL is created based on the configuration provided in the above image (API method-  `POST`, path parameter - `:customerId` and the API url - `tierForceUpgrade)`.
blocks.text: For example, the below API cURL is created based on the configuration provided in the above image (API method-  POST, path parameter - :customerId and the API url - tierForceUpgrade).

blocks.raw:
```json Trigger cURL

        curl --location --request POST 'https://eu.api.capillarytech.com/x/neo/:customerId/tierUpgrade' \
        --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
        --header 'x-cap-api-oauth-token: {token}' \
        --header 'x-cap-neo-test-variant-id: b48ddaab-a9d1-4419-b6cf-0a98d2596315' \
        --header 'x-cap-neo-dag-scope: org'
--data-raw '{
      "data": "add your json object here"
      }'
```

blocks.raw: ## Exposing a Neo API for B2C access
blocks.text: Exposing a Neo API for B2C access

blocks.raw: By default, a Neo API endpoint is accessible only via Intouch server-to-server authentication. To expose a Neo API for end-customer (B2C) access using an external CIAM token (such as AWS Cognito, Okta, or any OIDC-compliant provider), the endpoint must first be whitelisted in `api_gateway_extensions`.
blocks.text: By default, a Neo API endpoint is accessible only via Intouch server-to-server authentication. To expose a Neo API for end-customer (B2C) access using an external CIAM token (such as AWS Cognito, Okta, or any OIDC-compliant provider), the endpoint must first be whitelisted in api_gateway_extensions.

blocks.raw:
> 🚧 **Whitelisting required for B2C access**
>
> Calling a Neo endpoint without this whitelisting returns a `401 Unauthorized` error at the API gateway, even if a valid CIAM token is provided. To whitelist a Neo endpoint for B2C access, raise a request with the Capillary product support team.
